blog/en/already-exhausted-will-exercise-.title: The more tired you are, the more 15 minutes helps
panels: I just want to lie down
After a day on your feet, you end up lying down with your phone on every break.
The brain is more tired than the body
That fatigue is neurological fatigue. Stress hormones wear out the hippocampus.
Change into comfortable sneakers and try a 15-minute walk or light run.
BDNF, serotonin and dopamine flow, giving you the strength for the rest of the day.

blog/en/carnivore-diet-for-better-brain-.title: First steps on a carnivore diet
panels: Some people are sensitive to plant toxins (oxalates, lectins).
A diet centered on animal foods lets the brain use ketones as fuel.
Start by balancing your fat-to-protein ratio and increasing water and salt.
Many say focus improves after the early side effects pass, but talk to a professional first.

blog/en/neuroscientist-anxiety-move-exer.title: Exercise that tames anxiety
panels: Neuroscientist Jennifer Heisz, who lived with anxiety, started from the same question.
Short high-intensity exercise; morning workouts for focus; walks in nature for low mood.
Strength training also supports the memory-guarding hippocampus and dementia prevention.

blog/en/why-we-give-up-diets-and-tasks-t.title: Giving up isn't a willpower problem
panels: Diets and put-off tasks keep slipping, and you end up blaming yourself.
The brain is 2% of body weight but uses 20% of its energy, so it always chooses to save.
Make the first step tiny and move right away with the five-second rule.
Managing the brain's energy itself changes your choices.

blog/en/raemian-gallery-a-part-of-home-i.title: Immersion starts with space
panels: At home, but my mind wanders…
Sometimes you're home but your mind is somewhere else entirely.
When immersed, the brain releases dopamine and sinks deeply into one thing.
A small space of my own
Create a space of your own filled with things you love.
Space affects immersion: that's the message of the exhibition and talks.

blog/en/ceramic-problem-unsolved-for-yea.title: A years-old problem, solved in three weeks
panels: There was a wall in ceramic engineering that researchers couldn't crack after years of effort.
Don't let go of the thought
Immersive thinking: hold one problem long and without a break, and the brain finds the answer.
Instead of giving up, keep increasing the time you spend thinking about just one problem.
It wasn't special equipment but a change in the way of thinking.

blog/en/why-diets-and-savings-plans-last.title: Three-day resolutions are an identity problem
panels: Diets and savings plans last three days, and we call it weak willpower.
Psychologist Oyserman's theory: when identity and behavior don't match, it's easy to quit.
Read difficulty not as "it's not for me" but as "it's hard because it matters."
Design your strategy to fit you, and the behavior lasts.

blog/en/five-minutes-a-day-why-the-brain.title: Why five minutes a day changes the brain
panels: You resolve every morning, but it keeps falling apart within three days.
Repeat a very small amount every day, and neuroplasticity creates real change.
Instead of notes that are just a few words, keep records organized by month, week and day.
The very process of recording what you do builds the power to think.

blog/en/emotional-reactions-and-speech-h.title: Attitudes were reflex circuits too
panels: Ugh! The words came out first
Hear a sharp remark, and a cutting reply flies out before you can think.
Conditioned reflexes: repeated emotional reactions and speech habits are automatic circuits the brain has learned.
Notice the short gap between stimulus and response, and you can pick another option.
Attitude isn't innate personality but accumulated reflexes. Small repetitions build a new circuit.

blog/en/why-affirmations-fail-even-after.title: How affirmations reach the brain
panels: You shout it every day, quit a few weeks later, and life stays the same.
The bigger the gap between who you are and the affirmation, the more the brain resists.
Write identity sentences in the present tense, first person, only slightly different from now.
The reticular activating system picks out information in that direction, building staying power.

blog/en/if-you-keep-doing-things-you-reg.title: Why does regret always come later?
panels: Late-night snacks, words said in anger, impulse buys. You repeat the same choice knowing better.
The amygdala moves before the prefrontal cortex, so action comes before judgment.
Create a gap with affect labeling, the 10-minute rule and implementation intentions set in advance.
If you already regret it, try reinterpretation instead of self-blame. Meditation calms the amygdala too.

blog/en/skip-the-5-minute-warm-up-and-co.title: The difference 5 minutes before and after a run makes
panels: Speeding up suddenly without a warm-up strains your muscles and joints.
The brain needs to get ready too
Wake it gently, and blood flow to the brain and dopamine and BDNF release continue evenly.
5 to 10 minutes of dynamic stretching before running; a cool-down and static stretches after.
Take care of preparation and recovery, and running's brain benefits stay fully intact.
